source.title: Cerebellar lesions at a young age predict poorer long-term functional recovery

confidence_rationale: Human evidence that damage timing dissociates outcome with the OPPOSITE sign to naive Kennard: cerebellar lesions inflicted younger (during a critical developmental period) produce WORSE long-term recovery than the same lesions later, controlling for tumour type/size/location, radiotherapy and deep-nuclei preservation. This is direct support for Q-088's core dissociation and for its 'or the reverse' clause -- developmental disruption and mature disruption need not agree, and which is worse is not fixed. Held at 0.55 because it is observational human clinical data (n=45, three age groups) and lesion-of-the-developing-organ is only a partial analog to develop-without-the-mechanism.
failure_signatures: Because early cerebellar damage was WORSE than late, the naive assumption that a mature lesion upper-bounds the developmental verdict is falsified -- a REE probe that reasoned 'mature lesion is tolerable, so develop-without will be at least as tolerable' would be systematically wrong for critical-period mechanisms.

Outcome depended on confounders (deep-nuclei preservation, radiotherapy) as much as on age; a develop-vs-mature dissociation can be manufactured or hidden by uncontrolled covariates, so a REE probe must hold the substrate/curriculum fixed across arms.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In 45 posterior-fossa-tumour survivors matched on tumour characteristics but operated at different ages, early age at cerebellar surgery independently predicted worse long-term daily, motor and cognitive functioning, supporting an early critical period during which the cerebellar 'learning machine' is essential -- a reversal of the classic Kennard expectation that younger brains recover better.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-088 asks whether disrupting a developmentally-necessary mechanism early (develop-without) gives a different verdict than disrupting it in a mature system (mature lesion). This study is human evidence that the two dissociate AND that the developmental disruption can be the more damaging of the two -- the exact 'or the reverse' case Q-088 names. It argues the develop-without protocol is not redundant with mature lesion, because for critical-period mechanisms the mature lesion can under-estimate the true cost.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is early LESION of a developing structure, not development-WITHOUT a mechanism from the outset -- a partial analog. It is also observational human clinical data with modest n and residual confounding, and cerebellar-tumour surgery carries collateral damage (radiotherapy) absent from a clean REE ablation. Transfers the direction-of-dissociation lesson, not effect sizes.
mapping.source_context: Human clinical cohort; 45 posterior-fossa (cerebellar) tumour survivors in three age-at-surgery bands; long-term health-related quality-of-life, ataxia, dexterity and full-scale IQ, with GLM control for tumour volume, radiotherapy, deep-nuclei preservation and assessment delay.

confidence_components.notes: Confounder-controlled but observational human data; value is the demonstrated REVERSAL of dissociation sign, which is decision-relevant for how a Q-088 probe is interpreted rather than for its magnitude.
